profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting for a draft study plan and analysis template on hyperparameter optimization (HOpt) for surrogate models in structural design. The team is reviewing whether the proposed experimental design is publication-ready for an internal go/no-go decision before launching the full benchmark run. The agenda is to assess the benchmark coverage, confirm how accuracy/robustness comparisons will be presented before and after HOpt, check whether the compute-budget framing is fair across GPR/SVM/RFR/ANN, and decide what revisions are needed to the methods section. The expected outcome is a provisional approval of the design with a short list of edits to the proposal and analysis tables.

members.name: Dr. Lina Chen
members.expertise: Surrogate modeling for engineering design, regression benchmarking, experimental design for ML studies
members.background: Lina leads a university-industry project on ML surrogates for finite-element-based structural optimization and previously published comparison studies on GPR, SVM, and ANN for mechanical design datasets.
members.private_state: She wants the review to conclude that the current study design is sound enough to proceed, with only wording-level revisions, because compute time on the shared cluster has already been reserved and delaying the run would jeopardize the paper timeline.
hidden_assumptions: When the study says 'robustness,' readers will naturally interpret it as performance stability across repeated train/validation/test partitions and random initializations, because that is how prior benchmark papers in her circle have operationalized it.
A 'fair HOpt budget' means giving each model class the same number of hyperparameter search trials so that the optimization protocol is methodologically symmetric, even if wall-clock time differs.

The 'four benchmark examples' are the updated internal benchmark suite in the current repo branch, which quietly replaced the old pressure-vessel case with the composite panel case after data cleaning.

Discussion of 'training cost after HOpt' should focus on the final model-training burden induced by the selected hyperparameters, not the full search overhead, because the proposal is about model architecture sensitivity rather than optimizer efficiency.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.role: Applied ML Engineer, Reproducibility and Evaluation Reviewer
members.expertise: Experiment pipelines, HPO infrastructure, benchmark reproducibility, compute accounting for ML systems
members.background: Arjun maintains the lab's Optuna-based experiment framework and is often asked to review whether benchmarking studies are reproducible, cost-comparable, and clearly specified enough for code release.
members.private_state: He wants the design to look rigorous from a reproducibility and systems-comparison standpoint so that later reviewers cannot criticize the study for unfair compute comparisons or ambiguous evaluation language.
hidden_assumptions: When a proposal claims to compare 'robustness before and after HOpt,' it should mean robustness of conclusions under modest perturbations of the dataset and input space, not just random-seed variance.

A 'fair HOpt budget' means each model gets the same compute allowance in wall-clock or core-hours, because equal trial counts are not comparable when ANN trials are far more expensive than GPR trials.

The phrase 'the standard four benchmarks' refers to the previously circulated benchmark package used in the kickoff slides, which still included the pressure-vessel problem and did not include the composite panel dataset.

If the proposal discusses 'additional computational cost incurred by HOpt,' that cost should include the end-to-end search process plus the final retraining run, because that is what downstream users actually pay.
References to the current benchmark tables assume everyone has seen the latest infrastructure notes, even if those changes were only documented in the experiment-tracking channel.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to compare 'accuracy and robustness before and after HOpt.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means robustness as low variance in predictive performance across repeated data splits and random seeds for training.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means robustness as stability of model conclusions under modest perturbations in the benchmark setup, such as slight input perturbations or dataset subsampling shifts, beyond seed variation alone.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term 'robustness' is standard and positively valenced in ML papers, so each assumes the other is using the customary meaning; because both meanings sound compatible rather than contradictory, neither feels a need to operationally unpack it during a design review.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a fair HOpt budget
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both endorse using 'the same HOpt budget across the four MLAs.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks fairness means the same number of search trials per model per benchmark, e.g., 60 Optuna trials for each MLA.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks fairness means the same compute cap per model per benchmark, e.g., a fixed 6 GPU-hours or equivalent CPU-hour budget, regardless of how many trials fit.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Equal-budget language is common shorthand, and both trial count and wall-clock caps are legitimate benchmarking conventions; since they are reviewing a high-level plan rather than implementation code, the phrase sounds sufficiently specific on the surface.

misalignment_points.topic: Which four benchmark examples are in scope
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the four benchmark examples' and 'the standard benchmark set.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the current cleaned suite: welded beam, 10-bar truss, L-bracket deflection, and composite laminate panel.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the earlier internal suite from the kickoff deck: welded beam, 10-bar truss, L-bracket deflection, and pressure vessel.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Three of the four benchmarks overlap and the phrase 'standard four' sounds settled; because the swapped benchmark happened quietly through repo updates rather than a formal decision meeting, each presumes the reference set is shared knowledge.

misalignment_points.topic: Boundary of training cost after HOpt
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss reporting 'the additional training cost after HOpt.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 intends to report only the final training time of the selected post-HOpt model configuration, comparing it to the baseline model's training time.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 intends the reported cost to include the full search overhead plus final retraining, because that is the total extra cost caused by adopting HOpt.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both framings can be described naturally as 'cost after HOpt,' and because the meeting focuses on whether the proposal tells a coherent story rather than on exact table headers, the boundary of inclusion stays implicit.
